name: Zokhuo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only classificatory refs (Lama 2012, Pelkey 2011); no grammar/phonology of Zokhuo found

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for zokh1238 (references: Chen Kang 2010; Pelkey 2011; Wang Chengyou 2003; Lama 2012; ISO CR 2007-113; Zhang Tingxian 2017; Yunnan Institute of Nationalities 1984; Lu Jinyu 1987). hh.bib language code entries checked for yzk.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No grammar, phonology or sketch listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); only overview/comparative/wordlist/socling items; the Yunnan 1984 and Zhang 2017 wordlist compendia carry a 'Wenshan (Dzoko)' point.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages: a study from the perspectives of shared innovation and phylogenetic estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: No mention of stress anywhere in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent/'accent' = 0 hits). p. 85: "Zuoke [dzu21khʊ33], also called Zuokuo [dzɔ21khɔ͡33a33], is spoken in Wenshan County.. It has 28 initials, 30 vowels (25 monophthongs and 5 diphthongs), and 5 tones (/55/, /44/, /33/, /35/, and /21/) (cf. YYFC 1983)." Data second-hand from YYFC 1983; sections 5.8.3.1.10 and 5.8.3.2.3 treat Zuoke-Polo subgrouping only.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula comparative lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any language; no Zokhuo phonology sketch (sketches cover Phola, Phuza, S. Muji, Hlepho, Azha only). General typology para p. 4: "most morphemes are still analytic and monosyllabic. The languages are also tonal and feature a basic syllable structure that is complex in terms of initial contrasts..". Zokhuo appears only in the Phowa-clade tone-class discussion (pp. 16-17: TC-1 /33/ unmarked with splits to /21/, TC-2 /55/ splits, etc., shared with Khlula/Hlepho).

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2007-113: create [yzk] Zokhuo. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic justification only (lexical similarity <60% with neighbours, non-intelligibility, immigration history). Cites Lu Jinyu 1987 and Pelkey 2008 diss. as sources.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011
sources.note: Only modern first-hand work with Zokhuo data (DXZ point); ch. 1 typological overview and ch. 5 phonology sketches (pp. 223-270) are the places a general Phula statement on stress vs tone would sit; ch. 6 has Zokhuo tone-class reflexes. Glottolog's hh.bib marks a PDF as 'delivered' to the editors, so a scan exists but not openly.
